MSFT.rationale: Microsoft presents a strong fundamental case: revenue growing 18.3% YoY to $82.9B, EPS +23.4% YoY, operating margins at 46.3%, OCF surging 26% YoY to $46.7B with 1.47x coverage of net income, and a fortress balance sheet with ~$38B net cash and 0.12 D/E. The valuation has de-rated meaningfully — PE at 29.9x sits in the lower quartile of its 25.4x–42.8x one-year range, representing ~30% compression from the Aug 2025 peak of 41.1x despite earnings growing 23%. This disconnect between accelerating fundamentals and multiple compression is the core bull case. However, material caveats temper the score below +0.5: (1) the $190B capex guidance for 2026 — $35B above consensus — compresses FCF and raises return-on-capital questions, with Goldman warning 90% of OCF consumed by AI capex; (2) loss of OpenAI exclusivity removes a key Azure differentiator; (3) Google Cloud growing 63% vs Azure's 40% signals competitive pressure; (4) the earnings yield of 3.3% remains below the 10Y Treasury at 4.41%, and oil at $98.38 (+52% in 90 days) creates data-center cost headwinds. The near-term catalyst is mixed — Q3 earnings beat on revenue and EPS but the capex shock drove a 5% selloff, and the May 27 EU sovereignty package is a potential headwind. Net: excellent franchise with elite margins and growth, de-rated to a more reasonable valuation, but capex intensity and competitive dynamics prevent a higher conviction score.
key_factors: Revenue $82.89B in Q3 FY2026, +18.3% YoY; EPS diluted $4.27, +23.4% YoY — strong top-and-bottom-line growth trajectory
Operating margin 46.3% (improved from 45.7% YoY), gross margin 67.6%, net margin 35.7% — elite profitability sustained
Operating cash flow $46.68B, +26% YoY, OCF/NI = 1.47x — cash conversion strong, no earnings quality concerns
Balance sheet fortress: $78.27B cash, $40.26B debt, net cash ~$38B, D/E = 0.119 — minimal financial risk
PE de-rated to 29.9x from 41.1x (Aug 2025), now in lower quartile of 25.4x–42.8x range — ~30% multiple compression despite 23% earnings growth
EV/EBIT at 22.7x (range 19.2x–34.1x), P/B at 8.65x (range 7.3x–12.6x) — all valuation metrics in lower half of range
AI business annual run rate $37B, +123% YoY; Copilot at 20M paid commercial seats with <5% penetration of 400M+ user base — significant monetization runway
$627B commercial RPO provides multi-year revenue visibility supporting demand-driven capex
Capex guided $190B for calendar 2026, $35B above consensus; Q4 capex >$40B — FCF compression risk and return-on-capital questions
OpenAI exclusive license ended; AWS and Google Cloud can now offer OpenAI models — structural negative for Azure AI differentiation
Google Cloud grew 63% YoY vs Azure 40% — competitive gap widening with Anthropic $200B commitment to Google
EU Tech Sovereignty Package (May 27) may restrict US cloud providers from sensitive government data — regulatory headwind for European public sector
Earnings yield 3.3% below 10Y Treasury 4.41%; oil at $98.38 (+52% in 90 days) creates data-center cost headwinds
RPO grew only $2B sequentially vs $233B prior quarter — questions about breadth of demand beyond OpenAI

sources_cited.excerpt: Microsoft's revenue grew 18% year over year… Azure and other cloud services surged 40%… Annualized revenue from AI altogether now stands at $37 billion, up 123%… $627 billion in commercial remaining performance obligations

The selloff was not about earnings quality. It was about the disclosed 2026 calendar capex plan of approximately $190 billion, which exceeded analyst consensus of $154.6 billion by roughly $35 billion, and the explicit attribution of $25 billion of that figure to component price inflation

Shares fell… after company said it anticipates Q4 capital expenditures of $40 billion, and said capex for the calendar year 2026 would reach $190 billion… Microsoft stock fell as much as 5% on Thursday
The commercial backlog barely increased sequentially ($2B gain vs. $233B prior quarter), with much of the growth attributed to OpenAI rather than broad-based demand
Microsoft's exclusive license to OpenAI's models has ended, allowing Amazon Web Services (AWS) to now offer OpenAI models to its customers
Google Cloud achieved 63% revenue growth in Q1 2026, significantly outpacing Microsoft Azure (40%) and Amazon AWS (28%)

The European Union is considering implementing regulations to restrict US cloud providers' access to sensitive government data as part of its upcoming 'Tech Sovereignty Package' to be presented on May 27
Goldman flagged that major cloud companies are spending ~90% of operating cash flow on AI capex, with combined hyperscaler capex now ~$670 billion for 2026
